facts.statement: Gastornis lived from the Paleocene to the middle Eocene epochs.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Paleocene – mid Eocene,

facts.statement: The genus Gastornis was first described in 1855 based on a fragmentary skeleton.
facts.quote: Gastornis was first described in 1855 from a fragmentary skeleton.

facts.statement: The name Gastornis honors Gaston Planté, who discovered the first fossils in clay deposits near Paris.
facts.quote: It was named after Gaston Planté, described as a "studious young man full of zeal", who had discovered the first fossils in clay (Argile Plastique) formation deposits at Meudon, near Paris.

facts.statement: When first described, Gastornis was considered one of the oldest known birds.
facts.quote: At the time, Gastornis represented one of the oldest known birds.

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope discovered Gastornis fossils in New Mexico in 1874.
facts.quote: In 1874, the American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope discovered another fragmentary set of fossils at the Wasatch Formation, New Mexico.

facts.statement: The first nearly complete skull and skeleton of Gastornis were found in Wyoming in 1916 and described in 1917.
facts.quote: In 1916, an American Museum of Natural History expedition to the Bighorn Basin (Willwood Formation, Wyoming) found the first nearly-complete skull and skeleton, which was described in 1917 and gave scientists their first clear picture of the bird.

facts.statement: Gastornis was an extinct genus of large, flightless birds living during the middle Paleocene to middle Eocene.
facts.quote: Gastornis is an extinct genus of large, flightless birds that lived from the middle Paleocene to the middle Eocene epochs of the Paleogene.

facts.statement: Most Gastornis fossils come from Europe, though species have also been reported from North America and Asia.
facts.quote: Most known fossils have been recovered from Europe, although species historically assigned to the genus have also been reported from North America and Asia.

facts.statement: Gastornis is generally classified as related to the Galloanserae, which includes modern waterfowl and gamebirds.
facts.quote: Gastornis is generally considered to be related to the Galloanserae, the clade comprising modern waterfowl and gamebirds.

facts.statement: The largest species, G. giganteus, stood about 2.15 meters tall and weighed between 175 and 225 kilograms.
facts.quote: The largest-known species, G. giganteus would have reached about 2.15 m in maximum height, and weighed up to 175 - 225 kg in mass.

facts.statement: The skull of G. giganteus was huge relative to its body and powerfully built.
facts.quote: The skull of G. giganteus was huge compared to the body and powerfully built.

facts.statement: The beak of G. giganteus was extremely tall and compressed from side to side.
facts.quote: The beak was extremely tall and compressed (flattened from side to side).

facts.statement: The beak lip of G. giganteus was straight and lacked the raptorial hook found in predatory terror birds.
facts.quote: The 'lip' of the beak was straight, without a raptorial hook as found in the predatory phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: G. giganteus had a relatively short neck made of at least 13 massive vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck was relatively short, consisting of at least 13 massive vertebrae.

facts.statement: Gastornis had vestigial wings with upper wing bones small and highly reduced, similar to cassowaries.
facts.quote: The wings were vestigial, with the upper wing-bones small and highly reduced, similar in proportion to the wings of the cassowary.

facts.statement: Evidence such as the absence of hooked claws and bone isotopic signatures suggests Gastornis was likely herbivorous, feeding on tough plants and seeds.
facts.quote: This interpretation has since been questioned by several lines of evidence. The absence of hooked claws in known Gastornis footprints, together with analyses of its beak morphology and the isotopic signatures of its bones, suggests that it was more likely herbivorous, feeding primarily on tough plant material and seeds.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Diatryma is a junior synonym of Gastornis or a distinct valid genus.
facts.quote: Several genera, including the well-studied Diatryma, have traditionally been regarded as junior synonyms of Gastornis. This classification has been challenged by more recent studies, however, and some researchers regard Diatryma as a distinct and valid genus.

facts.statement: Scientists debate the synonymy of Gastornis and Diatryma because detailed comparisons of type specimens have not yet been completed.
facts.quote: Some subsequent studies either continued to use the genus Diatryma or argued against the synonymy, since a detailed comparison of type specimens has not been done yet and notable differences can be found in the species originally assigned to Diatryma from the type species of Gastornis.

facts.statement: In 2020, a distinct species named G. laurenti was described based on specimens found near Saint-Papoul, southwestern France, making it the most recently described species of Gastornis.
facts.quote: In 2020, however, additional specimens from this location were identified as a distinct species and named G. laurenti, making them the most recently described species of Gastornis.

facts.statement: Gastornis giganteus, formerly known as Diatryma gigantea, dates from the middle Eocene of western North America.
facts.quote: Gastornis giganteus (Cope, 1876), formerly Diatryma gigantea, dates from the middle Eocene of western North America.

facts.statement: The species Gastornis giganteus was named in honor of T. C. von Storch, who discovered the fossils during the Princeton 1927 Expedition.
facts.quote: The species was named in honor of T. C. von Storch, who found the fossils remains in Princeton 1927 Expedition.

facts.statement: Louchart et al. (2021) argued that there is no unambiguous evidence to support the synonymy of Omorhamphus storchii with Gastornis giganteus due to a lack of definitive juvenile specimens.
facts.quote: Louchart et al. (2021) argued that no definitive juvenile specimens of G. giganteus are known and that the two taxa have no known association, so there is no unambiguous evidence to support this synonymy.

facts.statement: Studies of calcium isotopes in Gastornis bones by Thomas Tutken and colleagues found no evidence of meat in its diet.
facts.quote: Studies of the calcium isotopes in the bones of specimens of Gastornis by Thomas Tutken and colleagues showed no evidence that it had meat in its diet.

facts.statement: Huge eggshell fragments were found in Late Paleocene deposits in Spain and early Eocene deposits in France.
facts.quote: Shell fragments of huge eggs have turned up in Late Paleocene deposits of Spain and early Eocene deposits of France, namely in Provence.

facts.statement: The largest known Gastornis footprint impression measured 40 cm in length.
facts.quote: The largest of these footprints, although only consisting of a single toe's impression, was 40 cm long.

facts.statement: Tracks dated to about 53.7 million years old suggest they were made by Gastornis.
facts.quote: The anatomy and age (about 53.7 Ma old) of the tracks suggest that the track maker was Gastornis.

facts.statement: The absence of raptor-like claws supports the hypothesis that Gastornis was a herbivore rather than a predator or scavenger.
facts.quote: Although these birds have long been considered to be predators or scavengers, the absence of raptor-like claws supports earlier suggestions that they were herbivores.

facts.statement: A single isolated feather found in the Green River Formation resembles the broad, vaned body feathers of flighted birds.
facts.quote: A second possible Gastornis feather has since been identified, also from the Green River Formation. Unlike the filamentous plant material, this single isolated feather resembles the body feathers of flighted birds, being broad and vaned.

facts.statement: The earliest Gastornis fossils come from Europe, suggesting the genus likely originated there.
facts.quote: The earliest (Paleocene) fossils all come from Europe, and it is likely that the genus originated there.

facts.statement: During the Paleocene, Gastornis was the largest terrestrial tetrapod on the island continent of Europe.
facts.quote: Europe in this epoch was an island continent, and Gastornis was the largest terrestrial tetrapod of the landmass.

facts.statement: The reason for the extinction of Gastornis is currently unclear.
facts.quote: The reason for the extinction of Gastornis is currently unclear.

facts.statement: Competition with mammals is often cited as a cause for extinction, though Gastornis lived alongside mammalian megafaunal herbivores in Asia and North America.
facts.quote: Competition with mammals has often been cited as a possible factor, but in Asia and North America Gastornis occurred in faunas dominated by mammalian megafaunal herbivores like pantodonts.

facts.statement: The genus Gastornis was described by Hébert in 1855.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hébert, 1855

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gastornis is Gastornis parisiensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Gastornis parisiensis

facts.statement: The species Gastornis giganteus was originally described as Diatryma by Cope in 1876.
facts.quote: G. giganteus (Cope, 1876 [originalmente Diatryma])

facts.statement: Gastornis is an extinct genus of large, flightless birds that lived during the late Paleocene and Eocene.
facts.quote: Gastornis es un género extinto de una gran ave no voladora que vivió a finales del Paleoceno y el Eoceno durante la era Cenozoica.

facts.statement: Gastornis species have traditionally been considered predators of small mammals.
facts.quote: Las especies de Gastornis eran aves de gran tamaño, y han sido tradicionalmente consideradas como predadoras de mamíferos pequeños.

facts.statement: Evidence including the lack of sharp claws and beak structure studies has led scientists to reinterpret Gastornis as herbivores that likely ate hard plant material and seeds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, distintas líneas de evidencia, incluyendo la carencia de garras afiladas en las huellas conocidas de Gastornis y los estudios de la estructura de su pico, han causado que los científicos reinterpreten a estas aves como herbívoros que probablemente se alimentaban de material vegetal duro y de semillas.

facts.statement: The largest known species, G. giganteus, could reach the size of the largest moas, with a maximum height of nearly 2 meters.
facts.quote: La mayor especie conocida, G. giganteus podía alcanzar el tamaño de las mayores moas, con una altura máxima de cerca de 2 metros.

facts.statement: The skull of G. giganteus was large compared to the body and of powerful constitution.
facts.quote: El cráneo de G. giganteus era grande comparado con el cuerpo y de constitución poderosa.

facts.statement: The beak was quite high and compressed, meaning flattened on the sides.
facts.quote: El pico era bastante alto y comprimido (es decir, aplanado por los lados).

facts.statement: The "lip" of the beak was straight, lacking a hook at the end like those seen in birds of prey and terror birds.
facts.quote: El "labio" del pico era recto, sin un gancho al final como el que se ve en las aves de presa y las forusrácidas.

facts.statement: The nostrils were small and practically positioned in front of the eyes, halfway along the skull.
facts.quote: Las narinas eran pequeñas y prácticamente posicionadas en frente de los ojos, a mitad del cráneo.

facts.statement: The neck was relatively short, consisting of at least 13 of these large vertebrae.
facts.quote: El cuello era relativamente corto, consistente en al menos unas 13 de estas grandes vértebras.

facts.statement: The wings were vestigial, with the upper wing bones being small and greatly reduced, similar in proportion to those of the cassowary.
facts.quote: Las alas eran vestigiales, siendo los huesos superiores del ala pequeños y sumamente reducidos, similares en proporción a los de las alas del casuario.

facts.statement: Gastornis was originally described in 1855 from a fragmentary skeleton.
facts.quote: Gastornis fue descrito originalmente en 1855 a partir de un esqueleto fragmentario.

facts.statement: It was named in honor of Gaston Planté, described as a "young scholar full of enthusiasm", who had discovered the first fossils in the deposits of the Argile Plastique formation in Meudon, near Paris.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado en honor de Gaston Planté, descrito como un "joven estudioso lleno de entusiasmo", quien había descubierto los primeros fósiles en los depósitos de la formación Argile Plastique en Meudon, cerca de París.

facts.statement: In 1874, American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope discovered another fragmentary collection of fossils in the Wasatch Formation of New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: En el año 1874, el paleontólogo estadounidense Edward Drinker Cope descubrió otra colección fragmentaria de fósiles en la Formación Wasatch de Nuevo México, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: He considered it belonged to a distinct genus and species of large terrestrial bird, and in 1876 named it Diatryma gigantea, from ancient Greek διάτρημα, diatrema, meaning "through a hole", referring to the large foramina (perforations) that penetrate some of the foot bones.
facts.quote: Él consideró que pertenecía a un género y especie distinta de ave terrestre grande, y en 1876 la denominó Diatryma gigantea, del griego antiguo διάτρημα, diatrema, que significa "a través de un agujero", en referencia a los grandes forámenes (perforaciones) que penetran a algunos de los huesos del pie.

facts.statement: In 1916, an expedition from the American Museum of Natural History to the Bighorn Basin (Willwood Formation) of Wyoming found the first complete skeleton and skull, which were described in 1917 and gave scientists the first clear idea of the bird's appearance.
facts.quote: En 1916, una expedición del Museo Americano de Historia Natural a la Cuenca Bighorn (Formación Willwood) de Wyoming halló el primer esqueleto y cráneo completos, los cuales fueron descritos en 1917 y le dieron a los científicos la primera idea clara de la apariencia del ave.

facts.statement: Gastornis and its closest relatives were classified in the family Gastornithidae, and were long considered members of the order Gruiformes.
facts.quote: Gastornis y sus parientes más cercanos fueron clasificados en la familia Gastornithidae, y fueron durante mucho tiempo considerados como miembros del orden Gruiformes.

facts.statement: Starting in the late 1980s with the first phylogenetic analysis of gastornithid relationships, a consensus grew that these birds were close relatives of the lineage including ducks and chajás, the Anseriformes.
facts.quote: Iniciando a fines de los años 1980 con el primer análisis filogenético de las relaciones de las gastornítidas, comenzó a crecer el consenso de que estas aves eran parientes cercanas del linaje que incluye a los patos y los chajás, los Anseriformes.

facts.statement: A 2007 study showed that gastornithids were a branch that separated early from the anseriforms, and formed the sister group to all other members of that lineage.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2007 mostró que los gastornítidos eran una rama que se separó tempranamente de los anseriformes, y formaba el grupo hermano de todos los demás miembros de ese linaje.

facts.statement: Gastornithids are sometimes included in their own biological order, Gastornithiformes.
facts.quote: Los gastornítidos son a veces incluidos en su propio orden biológico, Gastornithiformes.

facts.statement: Upon recognizing the apparently close relationship between gastornithids and anseriforms, some researchers classified them within the anseriform group itself. Others restricted the use of the term Anseriformes only to the crown group formed by all modern species, and named the larger group including extinct relatives of anseriforms, such as gastornithids, Anserimorphae.
facts.quote: Al reconocerse la aparentemente cercana relación entre los gastornítidos y los anseriformes, algunos investigadores los clasificaron dentro del grupo de los anseriformes en sí. Otros restringieron el uso del término Anseriformes solo al grupo corona formado por todas las especies modernas, y denominaron al grupo mayor que incluye a los parientes extintos de los anseriformes, como los gastornítidos, con el nombre Anserimorphae.

facts.statement: The type species Gastornis parisiensis was named and described by Hébert in two articles in 1855.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Gastornis parisiensis, fue nombrada y descrita por Hébert en dos artículos en 1855.

facts.statement: Fossils are known from western and central Europe, dating from the late Paleocene to the early Eocene.
facts.quote: Es conocido de fósiles hallados en el occidente y centro de Europa, datando del final del Paleoceno a inicios del Eoceno.

facts.statement: It is generally accepted that there are at least five valid species of Gastornis.
facts.quote: Generalmente se acepta que hay al menos cinco especies válidas de Gastornis.

facts.statement: Gastornis giganteus, formerly known as Diatryma, dates to the middle Eocene of western North America.
facts.quote: Gastornis giganteus (Cope, 1876), anteriormente Diatryma, data del Eoceno medio del oeste de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The species Omorhamphus storchii was described from fossils found in early Eocene rocks in Wyoming.
facts.quote: O. storchii fue descrito de fósiles de rocas del Eoceno temprano de Wyoming.

facts.statement: The species was named in honor of T. C. von Storch, who found the fossil remains during a Princeton expedition in 1927.
facts.quote: La especie fue nombrada en honor de T. C. von Storch, quien halló los restos fósiles durante la expedición de Princeton en 1927.

facts.statement: Gastornis xichuanensis from the early Eocene of Henan, China, is known only from a tibiotarsus (upper leg bone).
facts.quote: Gastornis xichuanensis, del Eoceno temprano de Henan, China, es conocido solo a partir de un tibiotarso (hueso superior del pie).

facts.statement: A 2013 re-evaluation concluded that the differences between this specimen and the same bone in Gastornis species were small, so it should be considered an Asian species of Gastornis.
facts.quote: Una revaluación del fósil publicada en 2013 concluyó que las diferencias entre este espécimen y el mismo hueso en las especies de Gastornis eran pequeñas, y por lo tanto debería ser considerada como una especie asiática de Gastornis.

facts.statement: A long-standing debate involving Gastornis is the interpretation of its diet.
facts.quote: Un debate de largo plazo que ha involucrado a Gastornis es la interpretación de su dieta.

facts.statement: It has frequently been represented as a predator of contemporary small mammals, the most famous of which is the primitive horse Eohippus.
facts.quote: Con frecuencia se lo ha representado como un depredador de los mamíferos pequeños contemporáneos, de los cuales el más conocido es el caballo primitivo Eohippus.

facts.statement: It may also have used its strong beak to eat large or very hard vegetation.
facts.quote: También pudo haber usado su fuerte pico para comer vegetación grande o muy dura.

facts.statement: Biomechanical analyses of the skull suggest that the musculature for closing the jaw was enormous.
facts.quote: Los análisis biomecánicos del cráneo sugieren que la musculatura para cerrar la mandíbula era enorme.

facts.statement: Both traits suggest that Gastornis could generate a powerful bite.
facts.quote: Ambos rasgos sugieren que Gastornis podía generar una poderosa mordida.

facts.statement: Studies of calcium isotopes in Gastornis specimens conducted by Thomas Tutken and colleagues did not show the presence of meat in their diet.
facts.quote: Los estudios de los isótopos de calcio en los huesos de los especímenes de Gastornis llevados a cabo por Thomas Tutken y colaboradores no han mostrado la presencia de carne en su dieta.

facts.statement: In late Paleocene deposits in Spain and early Eocene deposits in France, fragments of large eggshells have been recovered, for example in Provence.
facts.quote: En los depósitos de finales del Paleoceno de España y del Eoceno inferior de Francia, se han recuperado fragmentos de cascarones de grandes huevos, por ejemplo en Provence.

facts.statement: These were described as the ootaxon Ornitholithus and are presumably from Gastornis.
facts.quote: Estos fueron descritos como el ootaxón Ornitholithus y presumiblemente son de Gastornis.

facts.statement: The parent group of Gastornis is Gastornithidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gastornithidae

facts.statement: The family of Gastornis is Gastornithidae.

facts.statement: The time range of Gastornis is from the Selandian to the Ypresian, between 61.66 and 48.07 million years ago.
